threads.body: [Javaagent] A pipeline can receive `WRONGTYPE` for one command and then throw `JedisConnectionException` while reading a later reply. Completion selects the connection exception, but `captureServerErrors` still copies the earlier reply, causing both the span and duration metric to report `error.type=WRONGTYPE`. Apply the captured reply only when the batch returns normally or the escaping exception is the captured server exception, so terminal client failures retain exception-class classification.

[Javaagent] Jedis 2.3–2.x cluster commands bypass the new reply handoff. `JedisConnectionInstrumentation.AdviceScope.end()` sends their request to `JedisClusterCommandContext.capture()` instead of `endIfNotAttached()`, leaving the common reply context without a request to update. Cluster completion then ends the separate request, so a terminal `WRONGTYPE` is classified by exception class on both the span and duration metric. Transfer the confirmed reply to the cluster-owned request before completion, without classifying successfully recovered redirections as failures, and add a failed-cluster-command regression test.

The latest-head review at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20792#pullrequestreview-5707845407 correctly flags unmatched reply readers. The first commit isolates getBulkReply/getOne/getStatusCodeReply/getIntegerReply and aggregate getAll reads in Jedis 2, but direct public getBinaryBulkReply(), getBinaryMultiBulkReply(), getRawObjectMultiBulkReply(), and getIntegerMultiBulkReply() calls still bypass ConnectionReplyAdvice. In Jedis 2.3.0 these methods call Protocol.read directly; in 2.9.0 they call readProtocolWithCheckingBroken(), which this module also does not instrument. A response builder can send GET for a list key, catch WRONGTYPE from one of these unmatched read APIs, and still contaminate the successful outer batch span and duration metric. Extend isolation to all relevant supported reply readers across Jedis 2.0 through 2.x without changing actual batch reply attribution. Reuse shared read boundaries where available, with compatible older-version coverage; do not assume all versions have the later helper.

Preserve the first attempt's correct pipeline and transaction connection ownership and drain completion, ordinary nested-command isolation, propagation of escaping/returned errors, and terminal-failure precedence. Jedis 3 already funnels reads through its newly instrumented readProtocolWithCheckingBroken(); do not add redundant Jedis 3 production changes without a concrete missing path.

Add focused regression cases for the omitted binary/multibulk read paths during response building, including a handled same-connection read after the outer drain and a separate-connection read. Avoid multiplying every existing parameter combination unnecessarily. Exercise the supported oldest and later Jedis 2 APIs through the existing suites where feasible.

Finish the original acceptance criteria in the existing tests: assert the outer batch span status as well as error.type and the corresponding db.client.operation.duration point; after a handled nested failure, verify a later successful operation has no leaked error attribution. The helpers added in Jedis23ReplyIsolationTest and Jedis30ClientTest currently check error.type only, and the new tests do not verify a subsequent successful operation. Keep assertions scoped to the batch instead of requiring unrelated low-level send spans to share its classification.

Run the relevant focused tests for the amended code and regression cases, applying the narrowest spotlessApply tasks before behavioral validation. Keep this follow-up limited to the remaining reply-attribution bug and its originally requested regression coverage.

threads.body: [Javaagent] During a standalone `Connection.executeCommand(CommandObject)` call, an application builder that catches a failing `nestedClient.get(...)` leaves that GET's span and duration metric successful, without `error.type`. The outer request owner remains installed during `Builder.build()`, so the nested command is treated as delegation and its span ends at send time, before the failing reply. Isolate request ownership across application builder execution while preserving internal delegation, and add an installed-agent regression for this caught nested failure.
